$comment: Mission 1.68 §0. Preconditions verified from git, canonical baseline measured live, and the SSH construct preserved rather than retired.

canonical_baseline.$comment: Measured live. Every counter matched §0 exactly.

requirement_registry.$comment: §33. Read from the repository artifact. Expected to stay at 15.

current_ssh_construct.$comment: §2. The SSH-identification construct is preserved. Its problem is reachability under the apparatus market as documented, not validity.
current_ssh_construct.proposition: the number of distinct public IPv4 addresses from which, during a predefined observation window W, TCP port 22 accepted a connection AND the peer emitted an identification string beginning with the literal prefix SSH- before protocol negotiation

why_a_construct_pivot_is_allowed.$comment: §1. Stated so a reader cannot mistake this for lowering a standard.
why_a_construct_pivot_is_allowed.the_construct_is_an_instrument_not_a_pro: The SSH identification predicate is not something SROS promises anybody. It was chosen to prove that two independently produced observations can witness one source-independent proposition, so the aggregator stops being algebraically identical to baseline B-2.
conditions_all_of_which_hold_here: product relevance remains explicit and is a gate rather than a preference
any selected construct is frozen BEFORE any value is retrieved
no previously observed value informed the candidate set
a construct is only selected with at least two named apparatus routes
why_a_construct_pivot_is_allowed.what_this_is_not: It is not a relaxation. A construct that no two apparatuses can measure teaches nothing about aggregation, and choosing a measurable one is selecting an experiment rather than weakening a standard.
